title: Wren and the Compass
premise: Lior Iversen has spent years ferrying contraband-free cargo up the Vessin River, staying small enough that no magistrate, smuggler, or debt collector bothers to remember their name. But when the monsoon tide drains the river and exposes a sea cave holding the lost seal of the drowned Magistrate's Court—a token that legally transfers all river authority to its bearer—Lior becomes the most wanted person on the water. Hunted by Corvane, a corrupt harbormaster who wants the seal to legitimize his toll empire, Lior must survive the storm season with a leaking hull and the reluctant help of Sable, a disgraced court clerk who once sentenced Lior's father. As the floodwaters rise, Lior must choose: destroy the seal and return to invisibility, or use it to bring justice to a river that has never known any—knowing power, once held, is never easily set down.
about_author: August Villalobos is the pen name of a former barge hand who spent six seasons working inland waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people the maps forget, drawing on a lifelong fascination with rivers as places where law runs thin.

chapters.title: The Tide Takes Something Back
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Running low-season cargo, Lior navigates the drained Vessin and spots a cave mouth no chart records. Inside they find the Magistrate's Seal—and Sable, half-drowned, clutching a warrant for its recovery. When Corvane's patrol boat appears, Lior flees with both stranger and seal aboard. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread; the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the River Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Sable POV. Hiding in flooded backchannels, Sable reveals the seal's legal power and her role in convicting Lior's father on Corvane's forged evidence. The boat springs a leak; trust springs alongside it as they patch both. Corvane posts a bounty. Beat: resentment thawing into alliance, each recognizing the other's wound.

chapters.title: Monsoon at the Tollgate
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, shifting to Lior for the climax. Cornered at Corvane's toll fortress during the storm's peak, Lior is captured while Sable escapes with the seal. Offered freedom in exchange for the seal, Lior instead publicly denounces Corvane's forged convictions before the assembled boatfolk. Beat: the climax—love and duty collide as Sable returns, choosing Lior over the law she served.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Shared POV. With Corvane arrested by his own clerks using testimony Sable notarizes, Lior holds the seal over the floodwater—the river's future in one hand. They let it sink, choosing earned justice over conferred power, and sail out with the fleet behind them. Beat: resolution; power refused, love chosen, and a captain finally willing to stop moving.
